# AWS IAM Credentials Provider Extension

<!-- status autogenerated section -->
| Status        |           |
| ------------- |-----------|
| Stability     | [development]: extension |
| Distributions | [] |
<!-- end autogenerated section -->

This extension supplies short-lived **AWS RDS/Aurora IAM database authentication
tokens** to connection-oriented receivers through the core
[`config/configcredentials`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector/tree/main/config/configcredentials)
framework.

It is a **connection-credentials provider**, not a transport authenticator. Unlike
the `extensionauth` extensions (`sigv4auth`, `basicauth`, …) that sign or
authenticate outgoing HTTP/gRPC requests, this extension produces the
**username/secret a database driver uses to open a connection** — here, an RDS IAM
auth token used in place of a static password.

## How it works

The extension is **config-less**. It is declared once, listed in
`service.extensions`, and holds no per-connection state — its `Start`/`Shutdown`
are no-ops. Its only job is to advertise the `aws_iam` provider type so any
receiver can discover it via the host extension map, without importing this
package.

Each receiver supplies its **own** provider config inline (databases rarely share
credentials), resolves the extension at its `Start()`, and gets a `Provider` bound
to that receiver's config. The token is minted on demand via the AWS default
credential chain (ECS task role, EC2 instance profile, IRSA), cached per target,
and refreshed shortly before expiry.

## Configuration

```yaml
extensions:
  aws_iam:                       # declared once, config-less

receivers:
  postgresql/this:
    endpoint: this-db.123456789012.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:5432
    username: monitor
    credentials:
      aws_iam:                   # inline, receiver-owned config
        region: us-east-1
        endpoint: this-db.123456789012.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com:5432
        db_user: monitor
        # role_arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/db-access   # optional, cross-account

service:
  extensions: [aws_iam]
  pipelines:
    metrics:
      receivers: [postgresql/this]
```

Adding a second database is one more receiver with its own `credentials.aws_iam`
block — the single `aws_iam:` declaration covers all of them.

| Field      | Required | Description |
| ---------- | -------- | ----------- |
| `region`   | yes      | AWS region of the database. |
| `endpoint` | yes      | Database endpoint (`host:port`) the token is minted for. Supplied by the receiver. |
| `db_user`  | yes      | Database user the token authenticates. Supplied by the receiver from its username. |
| `role_arn` | no       | IAM role assumed before minting the token (cross-account access). |

The minted token is mutually exclusive with a static `password` on the receiver.
